get.description: Get the version of the binary consisting of Tag or Branch-name together with the commit-hash.
Get status of the service endpoint.

put.description:
Create a new access-token for the user of the current token, in order to extend the session.\
\
With `project_id` in the body, the new token is created for this project instead of the project of the current token, which switches the project without a new login. The user must be assigned to the project. The role within the project is read again in both cases, so changes of the role are applied with the renewal.

post.description: Create a new access-token for the given user-credentials. The token is scoped to the project given by the optional `project_id`, or to the default-project of the user, if not set. The user must be assigned to the project.

get.description:
Validate the access-token of the request.\
\
The check itself is done by the middleware, so a successful response means that\
the token is valid, and the content of the token is returned.\
\
`project_locked` is true, while the project of the token is locked by a backup or restore. The\
other components only allow reading requests of the user to a locked project.

put.description:
Create a new access-token of an admin for any existing project, also if the admin is not assigned to the project.\
\
Some components act on the project of the token, like isekai, when it restores a backup into another or a new project. The admin keeps the role within the project, if the admin is assigned to it, otherwise the token gets the role `admin`. The admin-flag of the user is read again from the database. This can only be done by an admin, the normal renewal of a token over `PUT /v1alpha/token` only allows projects, to which the user is assigned.
Change the passphrase of the user of the token for all future logins. The old passphrase has to be provided as well. Already existing tokens stay valid.
Set a new passphrase for any user for all future logins, without the need of the old passphrase. Already existing tokens of the user stay valid. This can only be done by an admin.

get.description: Get addresses and ports of all endpoints.

post.description: Create new project. This can only be done by an admin. Project-IDs starting with 'default-' are reserved for the default-projects of the users and are rejected.

lock.description: lock of the project during a backup or restore, None if the project is not locked

get.description:
List basic information of all projects from the database.\
\
Every project contains its lock, while it is locked by a backup, a restore or an admin. This can\
only be done by an admin.
List all users, which are assigned to the project of the token, together with the role of each user within this project.
List all users within a project, together with the role of each user within this project. This can only be done by an admin.

post.description: Add a user with a specific role to a project. A user can be added to the same project only once at the same time. This can only be done by an admin.
Remove a user from a project. A user can not be removed from its own default-project. This can only be done by an admin.

get.description:
Export a project together with its quota for a backup.\
\
Users and their assignments to the project are not part of the export, because a user can be member\
of multiple projects. Users, which are not admin, can only export their own project.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

post.description:
Import a project together with its quota from a backup.\
\
The project is imported under the ID of the path, so a backup can also be restored into another\
project. A project, which doesn't exist, is created with the name and the quota of the backup,\
which can only be done by an admin. An existing project is rejected with `409`, unless `force` is\
set: then its name is overwritten, and its quota only, if the user is an admin, so a user can't\
raise the quota of the own project with a backup. `quota_imported` shows, if the quota was applied.\
Users and their assignments to the project are never changed. Users, which are not admin, can only\
import into their own project.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

Lock a project for a job, like a backup or a restore. `reason` describes, why\
the project is locked.\
\
While a project is locked, its users can only read its resources, all other requests of users to\
the project are rejected by all components. Only the job, which has locked the project, can remove\
the lock again. Locking a project, which is already locked by another job, is rejected with `409`,\
so two backups or restores of the same project can't run at the same time. Locking it again with the\
same job is accepted. The nil-UUID is reserved for the lock of an admin and is rejected with\
`400`. Users, which are not admin, can only lock their own project.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

delete.description:
Remove the lock of a project, which was set by the job `job_uuid`.\
\
A lock of another job is kept and the request is rejected with `409`. Unlocking a project, which\
is not locked, is accepted, so the unlocking can be repeated. The nil-UUID is reserved for the lock\
of an admin and is rejected with `400`. Users, which are not admin, can only unlock their own\
project.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

post.description:
Lock a project manually.\
\
While a project is locked, its users can only read its resources, all other requests of users to\
the project are rejected by all components. Also no backup or restore can be started for the\
project. `reason` describes, why the admin has locked the project. The lock gets the nil-UUID as\
`locked_by_job`, because it belongs to no job, and it is only removed again by an admin with\
`DELETE /v1alpha/project/{project_id}/lock/admin`. A project, which is already locked by a backup or\
restore, is rejected with `409`. Locking a project again, which is already locked by an admin, is\
accepted. This can only be done by an admin.

delete.description:
Remove the lock of a project, independent of the job, which has set it.\
\
This is meant for a project, which stays locked after a failed restore, so it can be used again.\
The resources of such a project can be incomplete. This can only be done by an admin.

get.description: Get information of a project from the database. This can only be done by an admin.

delete.description: Delete a project together with its quota and the assignments of its users. Only projects without any resources and without users with the role admin or member can be deleted, so nobody can create a new resource during the delete. Observers don't block the delete. A locked project can not be deleted. The default-project of a user can not be deleted here, it is only deleted together with its user. This can only be done by an admin.

post.description: Create new user. This can only be done by an admin.

get.description:
List basic information of all users from the database.\
\
This can only be done by an admin.
Get information of a user from the database. This can only be done by an admin.

delete.description: Delete a user together with its default-project. The user can only be deleted, if its default-project contains no resources anymore. To prevent the creation of new resources during the delete, all users of the default-project are made observers before. The user is removed from all other projects, but these projects are never deleted. This can only be done by an admin.

put.description: Set the role of a user within a project. The user must already be assigned to the project. In its own default-project, a user can not be made an observer. This can only be done by an admin.

get.description:
List all projects, to which the user of the token is assigned, together with the role of the user within each of these projects.\
\
The default-project of the user is part of the list as well.
Get the quota of the project of the token from the database.

List basic information of all quotas from the database.\
\
This can only be done by an admin.
Get information of the quota of a specific project from the database.

put.description:
Update the quota of a specific project.\
\
Only the values, which are not 0, are applied, so single limits can be changed\
without providing all of them. This can only be done by an admin.

isekai.description: Orchestrator of the backups and restores. It is optional, so the clients still understand a miko, which doesn't know isekai yet.

MikoProjectExport.description: Project with its quota, like it is exported from miko into a backup. Users and their assignments to the project are not part of it.

id.description: ID of the project at the time of the backup

force.description: overwrite name and quota of an already existing project

project.description: project from the backup. Its ID is ignored, the project is imported under the ID of the path, so a backup can also be restored into another project.

created.description: true, if the project didn't exist before and was created by the import

quota_imported.description: true, if the quota of the backup was applied. The quota of an existing project is only overwritten for an admin, so a user can't raise the quota of the own project with a backup.

QuotaExport.description: Quota of a project, like it is stored in a backup.

lock.description: lock of the project during a backup or restore, None if the project is not locked

lock_reason.description: description, why the project is locked

locked_by_job.description: job, which has locked the project

reason.description: description, why the admin has locked the project

job_uuid.description: job, which locks the project. Only this job can remove the lock again.

reason.description: description, why the project is locked, like the backup or restore, which is running

lock.description: lock of the project, None if the project is not locked
lock of the project during a backup or restore, None if the project is not locked

ProjectRole.description:
Role of a user within a project.

The role is stored as lowercase string, which is the same representation as used by serde.

job_uuid.description: job, which has locked the project

Secret.description:
Wrapper around a string, which must not be leaked into logs or error-messages.

`Debug` and `Display` both print `***` instead of the content, so a secret stays hidden even when it is part of a bigger struct, which is logged as a whole. The content is only reachable through `reveal`, which makes every intended access visible at the call-site.

project_id.description: Project, for which the new token is created. The admin doesn't have to be assigned to it.
Project, for which the new token is created. If not set, the project of the current token is used.

project_locked.description: true, if the project of the token is locked by a backup or restore, so the user can only read its resources. It is not part of the token itself, because the lock changes, while the token is valid.
